{{Short description|Polish maskilic mathematician, poet, and author}}

'''Gabriel Judah Lichtenfeld''' ({{Langx|he|גַּבְרִיאֵל יְהוּדָה ליכטענפעלד}}; 1811, [[Lublin]] — 22 March 1887, [[Warsaw]]) was a [[Jewish-Polish]] [[maskilic]] mathematician, poet, and author. He wrote for ''[[Ha-Shaḥar|Ha-Shachar]]'', ''[[Ha-Tsfira|Ha-Tzefirah]]'', ''Izraelita'', and Polish newspapers, mostly on mathematical topics.<ref>{{cite EJ |title=Lichtenfeld, Gabriel Judah|first=Yehuda|last=Slutsky|url=https://www.encyclopedia.com/religion/encyclopedias-almanacs-transcripts-and-maps/lichtenfeld-gabriel-judah}}</ref>

==Biography==

A descendant of [[Moses Isserles]], Lichtenfeld showed early ability as a [[Talmud]]ic scholar. He later became familiar with [[Latin]], German, French, and [[Polish language|Polish]], and made a special study of philosophy and mathematics.

In the Hebrew periodical ''[[Ha-Shaḥar|Ha-Shachar]]'', there appeared a series of Hebrew articles by Lichtenfeld which attracted attention. His reputation was enhanced by his series of articles, in the Polish periodical ''Izraelita'', on Jewish mathematicians. Lichtenfeld is known also by his polemics with [[Hayyim Selig Slonimski]] on mathematical subjects. Among other works, Lichtenfeld was the author of ''Yedi'ot ha-Shi'urim'' (1865, "Science of Measurement"), ''Tzofnat Pa'neach'' (1874), a critical review of Slonimski's ''Yesode Ḥokmat ha-Shi'ur'', ''Tosefot'' (1875), a polemic against Slonimski, ''Kohen Lelo Elohim'' (1876), a book of mathematical criticisms, and ''Sippurim be-Shir ve'Shirim Shonim'' (1877, "Stories in Verse and Selected Poems"), a collection of poems and rimed prose by himself and by his son-in-law [[I. L. Peretz]]. Lichtenfeld's main book on mathematics, ''Bo'u Ḥeshbon'', was published posthumously in 1895.
